chunks.text: It all started with Mike Novogratz saying, “I identify as a wrestler.”
That sentence led to the intersection of $GLXY, Robinhood Chain and a financial system moving onchain.
That sentence had an account, a token, and a market.
$WRESTLER launched on @o1_exchange, paired against a GLXY-linked Stock Token on Robinhood Chain.
Not Galaxy’s Superstate shares. Not Nasdaq GLXY. A crypto-native market formed around an onchain instrument that references the same public company.
The Wrestlers were wrestling and Mr. Novo saw that and chose to give a follow. Soon after that came the unfollow.
Galaxy Digital’s official account posted four words of its own. “Just dropped a follow 👀” — then followed @wrestler_galaxy. Next day, the follow was gone.
A follow is not an endorsement. A reply is not a partnership. An unfollow is not a verdict. It is part of the record. The record is messy. The story underneath it is not.
Industries merging, or at least touching. The wave is REAL. Pioneers like @VladTenev are betting big on it. Certain people you simply do not fade.
Tokenized stock DEX volume hit $4.3B in a week, up 127.8%, with its first $1B day. Robinhood held 66.3% of it.
Agents → compute → energy → capital. The brains get cheaper. The body does not.
An agent is a process, not a query. It plans, calls a tool, waits, tries again, spawns helpers, loops. Agentic workloads burn 100x the energy of a chat.
One side is capital: trading, lending, staking, tokenization, institutional rails. The other is compute: land, power, data centers, AI and HPC. Most firms pick a lane. Galaxy built across the gap.
In late 2022, with crypto in pieces, Galaxy bought a distressed Bitcoin mine in Dickens County, West Texas for about $65 million.
Cheap land. Cheap power. Then mining margins broke and the hookup outvalued the machines. CoreWeave became the tenant. A stranded hash farm became a factory for compute.
Novogratz has said demand for compute is not a cycle... it is a structural condition. Helios is that sentence in steel.
September 2025: @galaxyhq partnered with Superstate so stockholders could hold tokenized Class A common shares. Those are actual SEC-registered $GLXY stock. Not a wrapper.
Robinhood built a different door. Stock Tokens. 24/7 venues. Weekend volume while Nasdaq is closed. Two approaches. One direction.
Superstate shares are registered common stock on the shareholder register. Robinhood Stock Tokens generally give economic exposure through a contractual claim. Different legal form. Different rails.
Once a public-market name exists on programmable rails, more than price charts form around it. Applications. Liquidity. Communities. Agents. Culture.
A sentence became a lore. The story became a meme. The meme became a community. The community went onchain.
On September 15, @altcoinist burned 50 million $WRESTLER — 5% of supply — from his own holdings. Round 2 fees bought back and burned another 3,333,333.33.
Combined running total burnt: 87.57 million tokens = 8.76% of supply.
The company at the center of the story noticed. Then it looked away.
Wrestlers can live with rules. What they cannot live with is a market that only exists when someone important decides to look.
If public markets are coming onchain, the first communities that show up should not have to pretend they imagined being seen. They were here.
We cannot tell you why the follows happened. We cannot tell you why the unfollows happened. We can only tell you the sequence.
Galaxy is the work-hour mask. WRESTLER is the overtime mask. One builds. The other carries the story after the glance.
The rails are real. The culture is already forming. And anyone who wants a seat can take one.
Never tap out is the new HODL. $WRESTLER.
Don’t let the inner caveman tap you out of the next 100x.
Prof. Enki is taking you back to prehistoric times...
Your amygdala still thinks a red candle is a sharp-toothed kitty in the jungle that wants you for breakfast.
We built cities, art, music, rockets. None of that updated the hardware. Deep down most of us are still running survival code.
Your amygdala has one job: keep the meat alive long enough to copy itself.
It does not know the difference between a 5% dump, a client ghosting you, or a tiger in the bushes.
Alarm goes off. Cortisol hits. Brain starts writing end-of-the-world fanfic.
It’s not a bug. That’s why Mr. Ugg-Zog-Tag didn’t get eaten, and why you’re here.
That same alarm makes you overtrade, revenge trade, tap tap early, or sit in cash and miss the whole tingggg.
Your life is usually not in danger. The circuitry never got the memo.
You don’t kill instinct. You notice it. Then you choose.
We survivalmaxxed by forming tribes. Not to vibe at the fire — because that is the only play that worked.
Lone wolves died. Small trust bands shared the meat, watched each other’s backs, and didn’t fold when shit went down.
Status and reputation inside the group mattered because getting kicked out was a death sentence. That was the winning strategy for 300,000 years.
So that’s how I invest. Simple and cavemanmaxxed.
TA is only layer 5-7 for me. Layer 1 is people. A tight group with skin in the game and loyalty to the tribe compounds.
Money is just the scoreboard we invented over time. Evolution still picks the winner.
Delayed gratification. They keep their word. They show up after they get slapped. They make the group stronger instead of farming it. They never tap out.
That’s why $WRESTLER is my highest conviction bag since TIBBIR (1400x) and SHIB (8000x). Same pattern.
Do patterns predict the future? No. (kinda) I’m fine being wrong in public. That’s the game.
You don’t need to be right every time. You need an edge. Even 1% compounds if you don’t tap.
Treasury fees bought back and burned supply. First burn was 6,767,676 🤼.
Then the lore got stoopid in the best way.
@novogratz follows the $WRESTLER account after they posted a real biography on his life. No AI slop.
Chart rips to ~5-6 mil. Minutes later, unfollow. Wick looks like Nightmare on Elm Street.
Next day it’s not the CEO but the nasdaq-listed @galaxyhq: “Dropped you a follow” and a handshake. A day later, unfollow again.
A regular meme would have tapped out at the first unfollow. GC would have went quiet.
$WRESTLER stabilized 2x higher than where it was pre-follow. Show’s on. 🍿
The top holder @Altcoinist doubles down and burns 50,000,000 of his own bag. That’s 5% of supply. $70K. It’s onchain.
People are still in the ring. Getting up. Not tapping out.
The whole groupchat is changing their PFPs to the @Nakamigos wrestler and round 4 is here.
SHIB had the same cultish pattern. Elon tweeted he doesn’t own it — SHIB nuked, then got back up. The dog people never tapped out.
Then TIBBIR. Community active every day for two years. One reply nuked the chart 60-70%. Beside a few jeets, same cultish energy is forming with $WRESTLER.
$WRESTLER is full of TIBBIR chads.
This industry spent 6 years turning me into a wrestler anyway.
“Never tap out” is not a slogan. It’s the opposite of what your nervous system wants when the candle goes red.
Wrestlers shared the meat. Sent bags to frens so they don’t tap out early. Burned supply instead of dumping it on the tribe.
Choose your tribe accordingly. C.Y.T.A
The test rounds only made the community bigger. The wrestlers keep standing up.
I’m betting on the oldest strategy we got. Round 4. Never tap out. 🤼
Identify as a $WRESTLER.
